title: 1998 AMC 8 Problem 19
statement: Tamika selects two different numbers at random from the set \(\{8,9,10\}\) and adds them. Carlos takes two different numbers at random from the set \(\{3,5,6\}\) and multiplies them. What is the probability that Tamika’s result is greater than Carlos’ result?

solutions.text:
Tamika can get \(17,\) \(18,\) or \(19,\) and Carlos can get \(15,\) \(18,\) or \(30.\)

The nine equally likely pairs are formed by choosing one result from each person. Tamika’s result is greater in \((17,15),\) \((18,15),\) \((19,15),\) and \((19,18),\) so \(4\) of the \(9\) pairs work.

Thus, the correct answer is A .
hints: List Tamika’s possible sums and Carlos’ possible products.
Count the favorable ordered pairs among the nine equally likely pairs.
